method.migrations: backend Flyway V1 through V12 at target dev d856d108; byte/path set unchanged from ed2cf742
caveats: Synthetic value lengths and distributions approximate the current private vehicle_id path and omit plate_number.
The required migration provenance and ingestion_origin columns/indexes do not yet exist and are not included.
Local Docker timing is a lower bound, not an academy RDS performance result.

sourceRowsToImport.derivation: immutable base 142,129/2,324,399 plus route-specific terminal catch-up 7,064/136,909; terminal target-overlap and quota-failure S3 rows are excluded

persistentBytesCurrentSchemaRange.includes: measured heap/index size plus current rows, table free space, and moderate bloat
persistentBytesCurrentSchemaRange.excludes: WAL, backups, snapshots, temporary files, derived forecast/statistics tables, and required new provenance/origin indexes

rsyncAndRemoteHashExpectedMinutes.basis: approximately 20-26 MB compressed base archive; actual SSH throughput not measured

rdsImportExpectedMinutes.basis: 2.61 million logical inserts, six current observation indexes, six current batch indexes, network/WAL/checkpoint overhead, and a burstable micro instance

t4gMicroRisks: The burstable class has only 2 vCPUs and 1 GiB RAM. RDS runs db.t4g in Unlimited mode, so sustained load can consume surplus credits/cost while competing with live traffic; CPU credit metrics must be watched.
One GiB database memory makes cache churn and checkpoint/WAL pressure material at this index volume.
The current online pending-forecast query would see every imported successful batch unless ingestion_origin gating is implemented first.
The existing vehicle_id indexes already account for direct private identity, while the new provenance/origin indexes add further write amplification.
Large transactions increase WAL retention, recovery time, and rollback cost; commit at no more than 10,000 observation rows.
Import concurrency must remain one and must yield to live collection latency/connection-pool pressure.
